sources.title: Immigration and General Services
sources.publisher: Ministry of Revenue and Customs, Government of Tonga
sources.officialityEvidence: The live central Ministry of Revenue and Customs page identifies itself as Government of Tonga and was last modified 20 August 2026. Its server presents an incomplete TLS issuer chain, so the page was reopened only with certificate-validation bypass; that is retained as a confidence risk.
sources.supportingExcerpt: Citizens of all other countries need visas to enter Tonga prior to arrival.

sources.title: Application for a Tongan Visitor's Permit and Entry Visa Checklist
sources.publisher: Ministry of Foreign Affairs, Kingdom of Tonga
sources.officialityEvidence: The current government-hosted three-page Ministry of Foreign Affairs Visitor's VISA PDF was last modified on the official host in May 2025. It expressly identifies a pre-arrival letter format for passport holders from Non-Waiver Countries.
sources.supportingExcerpt: Non-Waiver Countries, issued in a letter format prior to arrival

sources.title: Visas
sources.publisher: Embassy of the Kingdom of Tonga in the People's Republic of China
sources.officialityEvidence: The live official Embassy page publishes a broader competing visitor-arrival list, but expressly carries a Copyright 2018 footer and does not provide a later effective date or reconcile its list with the central 2025/2026 sources.
sources.supportingExcerpt: They will be issued upon arrival with a visitor’s visa for 31 days, free of charge.

sources.title: Immigration Act, Chapter 10.01 (revised legislation)
sources.publisher: Attorney General’s Office, Kingdom of Tonga
sources.officialityEvidence: Tonga's Attorney General publishes the revised Immigration Act. It grants immigration officers visitor-permit and visa powers but does not publish a current nationality schedule; the newer central Ministry sources supply the relevant nationality and timing rules.
sources.supportingExcerpt: A visitor permit may be issued at the discretion of an immigration officer.

policies.title: Swiss ordinary passport: visitor visa issued on arrival
policies.summary: Tonga Revenue's current named country cohort expressly includes Switzerland among travellers who may be issued a 30-day visitor visa on arrival.
conditions: The current Revenue source says the visitor visa may be issued on arrival for 30 days, subject to a valid return ticket to a country the traveller may enter and sufficient funds.

This is an arrival-issued visitor visa, not visa-free access or a pre-travel eVisa. Work, business, study, residence, diplomatic, official, service, and special-document routes remain outside this ordinary-passport visitor baseline.
The legacy Embassy page claims a longer Schengen-linked benefit, but its stated 2018 publication context is not controlling against the central current source.

policies.title: Non-waiver ordinary passports: Entry Visa required before arrival
policies.summary: Tonga Revenue states every country outside its current named arrival cohort needs a visa before arrival, while the current Ministry of Foreign Affairs Visitor's VISA checklist describes that non-waiver Entry Visa as issued in a letter format before arrival.
conditions: The current Revenue page supplies the complete residual rule: citizens of all other countries need visas before arrival.

The Ministry of Foreign Affairs checklist expressly identifies an Entry Visa for Non-Waiver Countries issued as a letter before arrival. This is an advance visa route, not electronically issued eVisa or walk-up visa on arrival.
The legacy 2018 Embassy list names several additional visitor-arrival countries but does not reconcile its broader list with the central 2025/2026 sources; it is not used to widen the current cohort.
Return ticket, funds, purpose, work/business/study restrictions, immigration discretion, special documents, and final admission remain conditions outside the baseline.
